neighbours.label: Next-word prediction of an uncommon verb starting with 'd', above all 'dined': fires on the word just before the slot when the context makes such a verb likely (people about to dine out or sit down to an evening or formal meal; also someone about to have dabbled in a hobby or dangled something). It sits on the slot, not on the d-verb itself, and stays low where the likely next verb is an everyday one or does not start with d (ate quickly, fed a baby, ducked, dozed).
fire: On the evening of their anniversary, the couple dined by candlelight at a quiet restaurant overlooking the harbor.
After the opera, the ambassador and his guests dined in the grand hall of the embassy.
We dressed in our finest clothes and dined at the captain's table on the last night of the cruise.
The king and queen dined with the visiting delegation beneath crystal chandeliers.
Having booked a table weeks in advance, they finally dined at the famous chef's restaurant downtown.
Every Saturday night, my grandparents dined out at the same little Italian place on Main Street.
Before the gala began, the board members dined together in a private room upstairs.
In his twenties he briefly dabbled in watercolor painting before turning to sculpture.
quiet: Every morning before work I quickly swallow a bowl of cereal.
A bishop’s church is called a cathedral because the Bishop teaches sitting in a large throne-like, called a cathedra in Latin.
Running late for the bus, she gulped down a granola bar on the sidewalk.
After the opera, the ambassador and his guests walked back to the embassy in the rain.
The nurse fed the baby a warm bottle of milk at three in the morning.
We grabbed a slice of pizza from the corner shop on our way to the game.
When the ball flew toward him, the boy ducked behind the fence.
Tired after lunch, grandpa dozed in his armchair by the window.
